plan:
- Microcontroller: ESP32 board for sensor reading and actuator control.
- Sensors: Soil moisture sensor (capacitive or resistive) and DHT11/DHT22 for ambient temperature/humidity.
- Actuators: Small 5V/12V DC water pump with a relay module, and a 5V/12V DC fan with a transistor/relay for control.
- Power: Suitable power supply (e.g., 5V/2A or 12V/1A) and a breadboard/protoboard for connections.
- Structure: Small greenhouse frame (e.g., mini polycarbonate or PVC frame) to house plants and components.
- Custom Parts: 3D-printed enclosures for ESP32 and electronics, sensor mounts, and fan/pump brackets.

examples.title: ESP32 Relay Module Tutorial
examples.description: A comprehensive tutorial on how to connect a 5V relay module to an ESP32 and control it remotely using a web server. This example demonstrates basic wiring, ESP32 code for relay control, and creating a simple web interface to toggle the relay, suitable for controlling devices like a water pump.

examples.title: Control a Relay Module with ESP32 – Arduino IDE
examples.description: This tutorial provides a clear guide on connecting a 1-channel 5V relay module to an ESP32 and programming it using the Arduino IDE. It covers the pin connections (VCC, GND, IN) and basic code to switch the relay on and off at set intervals, illustrating fundamental control of a connected device.

examples.title: ESP32 Wi-Fi Smart Switch using a Relay Module
examples.description: Learn to build an IoT smart switch with an ESP32 and a relay module that can be controlled over Wi-Fi. This project demonstrates how to set up an ESP32 as a web server to receive commands and activate the relay, effectively turning any connected appliance (like a water pump) into a smart device.

examples.title: DIY Smart Plug using ESP32, Relay and Blynk
examples.description: This example shows how to create a smart plug using an ESP32, a relay module, and the Blynk IoT platform. It's a great demonstration of integrating the relay into a full IoT ecosystem, allowing control of the relay (and thus the connected pump) from a smartphone app via the internet.

subSteps.title: 3D print all custom mechanical components
Install M3 heat-set inserts into all designated mounting points on 3D printed parts
Cut water tubing to the required length for pump connections
Deburr and clean all 3D printed parts, then test-fit mechanical connections
Connect Solar Panel to Solar Charge Controller input terminals
Connect 12V Battery to Solar Charge Controller battery terminals
Wire Solar Charge Controller load output to 5V buck converter input and relay module COM pins
Connect 5V buck converter output to ESP32, DHT22 sensor, soil moisture sensor, and both relay VCC pins
Wire ESP32 data pins to DHT22 sensor, soil moisture sensor, and relay IN pins
Wire fan relay NO output to Cooling Fan, and pump relay NO output to Water Pump
Connect shared system ground from solar charge controller LOAD- to water pump - terminal
Perform continuity checks on all power and data lines to ensure correct wiring
Connect ESP32 to computer and upload initial firmware
Verify ESP32 boots correctly and serial output is functional
Test DHT22 sensor readings for ambient temperature and humidity
Test soil moisture sensor readings and analog input functionality
Actuate pump and fan relays individually and verify fan and water pump operation
Confirm solar charge controller is charging the battery and providing power to loads
Mount the Solar Panel Mount and Solar Panel to the exterior of the greenhouse frame
Mount the Battery Holder and 12V Battery to the interior base of the greenhouse frame
Mount the Electronics Enclosure to the greenhouse frame
Install ESP32, both relay modules, 5V buck converter, and charge controller into the Electronics Enclosure
Mount the Soil Sensor Mount and Soil Moisture Sensor in soil near plants, and the DHT22 Sensor Mount and DHT22 Sensor inside the greenhouse
Mount the Pump Bracket and Water Pump near the water source, and the Fan Mount and Cooling Fan to the frame opening
Attach the water hose to the water pump and route all cables, securing with zip ties for strain relief and organization

projectDescription: A smart greenhouse system automatically monitors soil moisture and ambient temperature/humidity using an ESP32. It controls a 12V water pump and cooling fan via relays to maintain optimal conditions, powered by a solar panel and 12V battery.

tools: Crimping tool (optional, for custom wire harnesses)
Utility knife / snips (for tubing and zip ties)
assumptions: Basic electronics knowledge and safety practices
Familiarity with 3D printing software and operation
Arduino IDE or ESP-IDF installed for firmware development
Access to a 12V power supply for initial testing (optional, can use battery/solar)
